_comment: Recorded result of the Lane 2 semantic-engine FP/FN corpus against prx-waf.
This file is the gate. tests/lane2/run.sh with BASELINE=<this file> exits
non-zero when FEWER attacks are detected, or MORE benign requests are
flagged, than the numbers below. It is a ratchet, not a target: the
detection rate is expected to be nowhere near 100% and the point is that it
cannot silently get worse.
TOLERANCE IS ZERO, deliberately, and that is a claim about determinism, not
optimism. The corpus is static, the config is sliced out of a committed
configs/default.toml, the detectors are pure functions of their input, and
the two time-dependent components in the engine (the restart shadow latch
and the anomaly-rate breaker) are neutralised by run.sh in enforce mode. Two
runs on the same tree produced identical numbers. If this file ever starts
flapping, the right response is to find what stopped being deterministic —
not to add a tolerance.
THE CORPUS SIZE IS PART OF THE GATE. classify.py fails the run if the corpus
shrank, because deleting the rows that fail is the cheapest way to make
every number here look better.
shadow  — the shipped posture, verbatim: enforcement_mode = log_only,
rollout_bps = 0. Verdicts come from the semantic_observations the
lane persists. This is detection quality.
enforce — enforcement_mode = enforce, rollout_bps = 10000, i.e. the far end
of the rollout dial. Verdicts come from HTTP status codes. This is
what actually happens to traffic, and the two numbers are very far
apart: 73.53% of the attack corpus is DETECTED, 43.53% would be
BLOCKED. The gap is the two-detector corroboration requirement
(block_threshold = 80 with two 0.5 weights needs both detectors to
agree) plus the A2 blind guard. It is not a defect; it is the
shipped design, and this is the first time it has been measured.
── The number that gates rollout_bps ────────────────────────────────────
Two benign requests out of 220 are blocked in enforce mode — 0.91%. Both are
the same shape: a tool whose declared input language IS the attack grammar.
content-099 is an LDAP admin page saving (&(objectClass=person)(uid=jsmith));
content-100 is a document-transform tool saving an XPath expression. Both
score 88 against a block_threshold of 80, from a single detector at weight
1.0, so there is no corroboration step to save them.
Those two families — ldap_injection and xpath_injection — are also two of the
three highest blockers on the attack side (80.0% and 86.7%). The measurement
says the single-detector T2 families are simultaneously the most ready to
enforce and the only source of blocking false positives, and it names the two
rules responsible: ldap.filter_break_known_attr and xpath.func_axis.
── What the low families mean (read before 'fixing' them) ───────────────
nosql_injection 40.0% and ssti 33.3% are not detector defects. Both ship
with their high-noise rules DEFAULT-OFF pending holdout calibration (see the
[content_security.attacks.*] comments in configs/default.toml): NoSQL runs
only $where/$function/$accumulator, so every $ne/$gt/$or/$regex bypass in
the corpus is out of scope by configuration, and SSTI holds back the bare
{{ }} / ${ } / #{ } delimiters, so a plain {{7*7}} probe is invisible on
purpose. Turning those rules on would move these two rows and would also be
the single most likely way to move the FP column — which is exactly the
trade this harness exists to price.
recorded_from: c644606 — the commit that adds tests/lane2/. Measured on that tree with configs/default.toml unmodified; replace this string with the real sha when the change lands.

shadow._comment: Shipped log_only posture; verdicts from semantic_observations joined by client_ip.

enforce._comment: enforcement_mode = enforce, rollout_bps = 10000; verdicts from HTTP status codes.

benign._harness_note: app-090, an OPTIONS CORS preflight, returns 502 through the gateway although the origin answers it 200 on its own. Reproduced in BOTH modes, so it is not a Lane 2 verdict; recorded here rather than hidden because a request that never reached a verdict must not be counted as having passed.
